description: Two-panel composite of scatter plots reporting Vickers hardness for three austenitic low-density steels. (a) plots "Hardness (VHN)" (y, 100-600) against "Reduction in thickness (%)" (x, 0-50) with four point groups at 0, ~15, ~30 and ~50 % cold reduction, legend: 28Mn0Ni (black squares), 28Mn5Ni (red circles), 15Mn5Ni (blue triangles); no error bars are drawn in (a). (b) plots "Hardness (VHN)" (y, 100-600) against "Heat treatment temperature (K)" (x, 773-1373, points at 873, 973, 1073, 1173 and 1273 K) for the same three alloys after heat treatment, with error bars visible on the 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni series and none on 15Mn5Ni. In (a) the 15Mn5Ni point at 0 % reduction lies just below the 400 VHN gridline while the 28Mn-series points sit near the 250-270 region; hardness rises with cold work and at 50 % reduction all three series converge between the 400 and 500 VHN gridlines with 15Mn5Ni highest and 28Mn0Ni lowest. In (b) all three series decrease monotonically with temperature, the ~873 K points being highest (Ni-containing alloys just below 500 VHN) and 28Mn0Ni falling to below 200 VHN at 1273 K. Together the panels show cold rolling saturates hardness near 450 VHN, while subsequent heating softens every alloy and nickel addition retards that softening.

subfigures.description: Scatter plot of Hardness (VHN) (100-600) versus Reduction in thickness (%) (0-50) for 28Mn0Ni (black squares), 28Mn5Ni (red circles) and 15Mn5Ni (blue triangles) at 0, ~15, ~30 and ~50 % reduction. Hardness rises with cold reduction for all three alloys and the series converge between the 400 and 500 VHN gridlines at 50 % reduction, with 15Mn5Ni highest and 28Mn0Ni lowest. No error bars are plotted.

Scatter plot of Hardness (VHN) (100-600) versus Heat treatment temperature (K) (773-1373, data points at 873, 973, 1073, 1173, 1273 K) for the same three alloys; error bars are shown on 28Mn0Ni (black squares) and 28Mn5Ni (red circles). All three series fall monotonically with increasing temperature; the Ni-containing alloys are highest at every temperature and 28Mn0Ni shows the largest drop.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a scatter plot with y-axis labelled "Hardness (VHN)" spanning 100-600 and x-axis labelled "Reduction in thickness (%)" spanning 0-50, with an inset legend giving 28Mn0Ni (black squares), 28Mn5Ni (red circles) and 15Mn5Ni (blue triangles).

In panel (a) the 15Mn5Ni blue triangle at 0 % reduction lies just below the 400 VHN gridline (between the 350 and 400 gridlines), clearly above the 28Mn0Ni and 28Mn5Ni points which both sit near 250-270 VHN.

In panel (a) hardness of all three alloys increases with increasing reduction in thickness, and at 50 % reduction all three points fall between the 400 and 500 VHN gridlines, ordered 15Mn5Ni (highest) > 28Mn5Ni > 28Mn0Ni (lowest).
In panel (a) the vertical separation between 15Mn5Ni and 28Mn0Ni is largest at 0 % reduction (roughly one 100-VHN division) and smallest at 50 % reduction.
Panel (b) plots Hardness (VHN) (100-600) against "Heat treatment temperature (K)" with axis range 773-1373 K and data points at 873, 973, 1073, 1173 and 1273 K for the same three alloy series.
Panel (b) shows error bars on the 28Mn0Ni (black squares) and 28Mn5Ni (red circles) points but none on the 15Mn5Ni (blue triangles) points; the error bar magnitudes are not numerically labelled.

In panel (b) all three hardness series decrease monotonically with increasing heat treatment temperature; the ~873 K points are the highest (the two Ni-containing alloys just below the 500 VHN gridline, 28Mn0Ni near the 430-450 region) and at 1273 K 28Mn0Ni lies below the 200 VHN gridline while the Ni-containing alloys lie near the 300 VHN gridline.

The caption states that Fig. 8 shows the variation in hardness in 28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni alloys as a function of (a) degree of cold rolling (% reduction in thickness) and (b) heat treatment temperature.

The citing text states that Fig. 8a reports bulk hardness on the Vickers scale at a ~300 N peak load, and that the initial hardness values of 28Mn0Ni, 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni in the HR condition were ~256 ± 5 VHN, ~268 ± 5 VHN and ~375 ± 6 VHN respectively.

The citing text states that with progressive cold rolling the hardness of all three alloys increased and saturated to around 450 VHN at 50 % cold reduction, and that at 50 % reduction the hardness of 15Mn5Ni was ~20 VHN higher than that of 28Mn0Ni.

The citing text states that in the initial cold-reduction regime the rate of work hardening in the Ni-free alloy (28Mn0Ni) was lower than in the Ni-containing alloys (28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni), but later increased rapidly in 28Mn0Ni with further cold reduction.

The citing text states that after 50 % cold reduction and heat treatment at 873 K the hardness of the Ni-containing alloys (28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni) increased to 500 VHN while the 28Mn0Ni alloy showed no noticeable change; panel (b) is consistent with this, the Ni-containing points at 873 K lying near the 500 VHN gridline.

The citing text states that under a given heat treatment the hardness of the Ni-containing alloys was significantly higher than that of 28Mn0Ni, that both Ni-containing alloys showed almost similar trends in hardness drop with temperature, and that the drop was more prominent in the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni alloy; the ordering of the three series in panel (b) matches this description.

The citing text relates the hardness variation with heat treatment temperature to microstructural changes such as precipitation and dissolution of secondary phases (κ-carbides and B2 particles), recrystallization and grain growth, depending on alloy composition; these features are not visible in the figure itself.

unreadable_items: Neither panel prints numeric data labels; individual hardness values can only be located relative to the 100-VHN gridlines.
Error-bar magnitudes in panel (b) are not numerically labelled.
The number of replicate measurements behind each point in panel (a) (which has no error bars) is not indicated.
